name: American Gothic
kicker: Grant Wood’s 1930 farm couple · One of America’s most parodied paintings
briefing: In 1930, Iowa artist Grant Wood painted _American Gothic_, showing a stern farmer gripping a pitchfork beside a woman in front of a small white farmhouse. Wood’s own sister and his dentist posed as the models, and the Gothic-style window on the house gave the painting its name. Now hanging in the Art Institute of Chicago, it has become one of the most recognized and most parodied images in American art.

tossups.p: This painting’s creator visited Munich, Germany, in 1928, where Northern Renaissance paintings shaped the crisp, detailed realism he later used here. He belonged to the American Regionalist movement alongside painters like Thomas Hart Benton and John Steuart Curry.
tossups.r: This work’s house was modeled on a small cottage in Eldon, Iowa, while its two figures were modeled separately back in the artist’s Cedar Rapids studio. For 10 points, name this 1930 painting by Grant Wood showing a farmer holding a pitchfork beside a woman.

tossups.p: This painting’s house is built in a style sometimes called Carpenter Gothic, a wood-frame echo of European Gothic Revival architecture. Its title actually comes from the pointed window of that style, set between its two central figures.
tossups.r: A small red barn appears off to one side of the farmhouse. For 10 points, name this 1930 painting of a solemn farm couple, created by Grant Wood.

tossups.p: When this painting debuted at a Chicago exhibition in 1930, it won a cash prize before the host museum acquired it outright. Many viewers back in Iowa felt insulted, reading it as mockery of rural Midwesterners, though its creator insisted he intended admiration, not satire.
tossups.r: Its two figures stand in front of a small white farmhouse with a pointed, church-like window. For 10 points, name this painting of a pitchfork-holding farmer and a woman, by Grant Wood.

tossups.p: The models for this painting’s two figures were the artist’s own sister and his dentist, who posed separately rather than together. That sister was about thirty at the time, roughly half the dentist’s age.
tossups.r: The woman’s cameo brooch may depict the Greek goddess Persephone, while the man holds a three-pronged pitchfork. For 10 points, name this 1930 painting by Grant Wood.

tossups.p: This painting blends sharp, precise realism with a flattened, almost folk-art simplicity, and some art historians note how its pitchfork’s three prongs echo the stitching on the man’s overalls and the shape of the house’s window. Its house was based on a small cottage the artist sketched on a visit to Eldon, Iowa.
tossups.r: A red barn and, in some descriptions, a church spire appear in its background. For 10 points, name this painting of a stern farm couple, created by Grant Wood.

tossups.p: The male figure in this painting wears round, steel-rimmed glasses and denim overalls while holding a pitchfork. The artist’s sister, Nan Wood Graham, insisted she was meant to represent the farmer’s daughter rather than his wife.
tossups.r: The dentist Byron McKeeby modeled for the male figure. For 10 points, name this 1930 painting of a solemn Iowa farm couple, by Grant Wood.

tossups.p: This painting’s creator visited Munich in 1928 before returning to Iowa and helping lead the American Regionalist movement. Its central house, a small white cottage, was inspired by a real building in Eldon, Iowa, that the artist happened to sketch.
tossups.r: A woman in a colonial-print apron stands beside a pitchfork-holding farmer. For 10 points, name this painting, one of the most parodied images in American art, by Grant Wood.

tossups.p: Some viewers from the artist’s home state felt this painting mocked rural Midwesterners as grim and puritanical, though its creator always denied any intent to satirize. The woman’s cameo brooch in the painting may depict the goddess Persephone.
tossups.r: A red barn stands beside a small white farmhouse with a pointed window. For 10 points, name this painting of a pitchfork-wielding farmer and a woman, by Grant Wood.

tossups.p: The pitchfork’s three prongs are echoed in the stitching of the farmer’s overalls and the shape of the farmhouse’s window behind him, a detail art historians often point out in this painting. Its creator posed his sister and his dentist separately for the two figures.
tossups.r: The house shown here was inspired by a real cottage in Eldon, Iowa. For 10 points, identify this 1930 painting of a severe-looking farm couple, by Grant Wood.

tossups.p: This painting won a cash prize at a 1930 Chicago exhibition, after which the host museum bought it for its permanent collection. Its creator belonged to the American Regionalist movement, alongside artists such as Thomas Hart Benton.
tossups.r: Its house is built in a wood-frame style sometimes called Carpenter Gothic. For 10 points, name this painting of a pitchfork-holding farmer and a woman, created by Grant Wood.

tossups.p: The sister of this painting’s creator modeled for its female figure at about age thirty, while its male model was in his sixties. She later insisted that the two figures were meant to be father and daughter, not husband and wife.
tossups.r: The male figure wears round glasses and overalls while gripping a pitchfork. For 10 points, name this 1930 painting by Grant Wood, now owned by the Art Institute of Chicago.

tossups.p: A dentist named Byron McKeeby posed for part of this painting, while the artist’s sister posed for the rest, each sitting separately in the artist’s studio. The house behind them was modeled on a small Carpenter Gothic cottage in Eldon, Iowa.
tossups.r: A red barn and a pointed window appear behind the painting’s two stern figures. For 10 points, name this 1930 farmhouse painting by Grant Wood.

tossups.p: This painting’s creator studied Northern Renaissance art during a 1928 trip to Munich, which shaped the crisp detail he brought to this picture two years later. Its title comes from the pointed window style of the house in its background.
tossups.r: The painting shows a farmer holding a pitchfork beside a woman in a colonial-print apron. For 10 points, name this painting by Grant Wood, one of the most parodied works in American art.

tossups.p: The cameo brooch worn by this painting’s female figure may depict the Greek goddess Persephone. The male figure’s round, steel-rimmed glasses and denim overalls complete a severe-looking pair standing before a white farmhouse.
tossups.r: That farmhouse, with its pointed window, is built in a wood-frame style called Carpenter Gothic. For 10 points, name this painting of a pitchfork-holding farmer, by Grant Wood.

tossups.p: Many Iowans were offended by this painting when it first appeared, believing it mocked them as grim and old-fashioned, though its creator denied any such intent. Its house was based on a real cottage in Eldon, Iowa, with a distinctive pointed window.
tossups.r: A farmer holds a pitchfork beside a woman in front of that farmhouse. For 10 points, name this 1930 painting, one of the most parodied images in American art, painted by Grant Wood.

trap.title: The painting or the painter?
trap.body: Grant Wood painted several famous works, including _American Gothic_, _Parson Weems’ Fable_ (which shows a young George Washington and a cherry tree), and _Daughters of Revolution_. A clue naming the farmhouse, the pitchfork, or the Gothic window wants this specific painting, not the artist himself or his other work.
trap.fix: If the clues describe a person’s whole career or several different paintings, the answer is “Grant Wood.” If the clues describe one farmhouse, one pitchfork, and one couple, the answer is this painting’s title.
